title: Trinity
definition: The Trinity is the doctrine that the one true God eternally exists as three distinct Persons: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.
summary: God is one in being and three in Person: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.
christFocus: Jesus reveals the Father, is Himself fully God, and sends the Holy Spirit, bringing believers into fellowship with the triune God.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The doctrine of the Trinity teaches that there is one God, not three gods, and that the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are each truly and fully God. The three Persons are distinct, yet they share the one divine being eternally.

The Trinity is not a puzzle invented by theologians; it is the Bible's witness to who God is. Scripture reveals the Father as God, the Son as God, and the Holy Spirit as God, while also teaching that God is one. Faithful doctrine receives all that Scripture teaches without flattening the mystery.

The Trinity matters because salvation itself is triune. The Father sends the Son, the Son accomplishes redemption, and the Spirit applies the work of Christ to believers. Christian worship, prayer, baptism, and discipleship are shaped by the triune name of God.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Without the Trinity, the church loses the biblical identity of God and the fullness of the Gospel. This doctrine protects believers from reducing Jesus to a created being, treating the Spirit as a force, or thinking of God in ways that contradict Scripture.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Worship the Father through the Son in the power of the Holy Spirit. Let the Trinity shape your prayer, your understanding of salvation, and your confidence that God has made Himself known truly, even where His being remains beyond full human comprehension.
